text: Curiosity: Ger. Neugier , Wissbegier ; Fr. curiosité ; Ital. curiosità . The disposition to give attention, so far as it has for its motive the mere increase of knowledge, apart from practical interest. ( G.F.S. - J.M.B. ) The two cases often distinguished (as in the German terms) are those respectively of curiosity and interest in novelty (Neugier), and the disposition to learn or to know for the sake of information (Wissbegier; cf. Groos, Die Spiele d . Menschen ), the latter being, however, usually motived by the somewhat trivial reason which characterizes curiosity in general. Literature : GROOS, loc. cit., 184 ff., also Die Spiele d. Thiere (Eng. trans.); JAMES, Princ. of Psychol., ii. 430. See the topic 'Interest' in the textbooks of psychology. ( J.M.B. )
